name: Ted Kennedy
summary: Edward M. Kennedy was a Democratic senator for 47 years who sponsored major health, civil rights, disability and immigration laws and pressed for universal health coverage and a higher minimum wage. He voted against the 2002 Iraq war authorisation, called for a moratorium on executions, and supported labour unions and abortion rights. He opposed school vouchers and Social Security privatisation.

abortion-legal.rationale: Opposed banning partial-birth abortion except to save the mother's life, and warned in 1987 that women would be forced into back-alley abortions.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Nulled: the only source is an OnTheIssues summary, which is not evidence; the Voteview search did not find the Contra votes.

arms-reduction.rationale: Called in 1983 for an immediate, mutual and verifiable nuclear freeze, and voted for the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty in 1999.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Nulled: the only source is an OnTheIssues summary, which is not evidence; his Voteview record has no 2009 stimulus vote on this question.

ban-cartels.rationale: Said in 1980 he would tame monopoly and close tax loopholes.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: His 2007 proposal prohibits funding an Iraq escalation without fresh congressional authorization.

close-ties-china.rationale: Nulled: the only source is an OnTheIssues summary, which is not evidence, and the China trade votes do not say he wants closer ties with China than with the United States.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Spoke for the Employee Free Choice Act: workers who choose a union get a fair process for a first contract, with mediation and, if that fails, binding arbitration.

collective-defense.rationale: Nulled: the only source is an OnTheIssues summary, which is not evidence; the NATO enlargement vote does not address an attack on one being an attack on all.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said in 1980 that the demands of the people were for better government, and that the President serves at the pleasure of the people.

corporate-influence.rationale: Voted Yea on the Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act (soft-money limits) in April 2001 and on the March 2002 votes.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Voted Nay on the 1977 Helms amendment barring federal funds for affirmative-action enforcement, to table the Hayakawa amendment on affirmative-action guidelines (1979) and to table a Helms amendment against affirmative-action cases (1977), keeping those programmes.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The oral history defends judges interpreting the law against intimidation and politically motivated removal threats.

death-penalty.rationale: Voted Nay on cloture and on passage (February 1984) of the bill creating a federal death penalty for the most serious crimes, Nay on the 1991 amendment imposing the death penalty for drug-related homicides in D.C., and Yea to table a 1988 death-penalty amendment.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Opposed the 1995 welfare overhaul and the 1996 block grants, and called the 2006 welfare reform bill legislative child abuse.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Nulled: the only source is an OnTheIssues summary, which is not evidence; no vote or remark of his on disparate-impact liability was found.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Joined reintroducing the Equal Rights Amendment (2007-03-27), saying commitment to equal rights for men and women should be in the Constitution and that it guarantees freedoms apply equally to men and women.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Nulled: the only source is an OnTheIssues summary, which is not evidence; the Voteview and Congressional Record searches found no vote or remark on drastic climate action.

economic-freedom.rationale: Mixed: he spoke of the free enterprise system being free in fact, and also of economic protections for workers.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Voted Yea on 17 May 2002 for the bill endorsing further enlargement of the NATO alliance.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Voted Nay on the 1977 amendment prohibiting HEW funds for enforcing affirmative-action programmes in college admissions, hiring and promotion, and Yea to table the 1977 and 1979 Helms and Hayakawa amendments against affirmative-action enforcement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said in 1979 he wanted freedom for black and brown people as well as white, and sponsored the Equal Rights Amendment in 2007.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: That speech makes preventing nuclear destruction of the planet an urgent public responsibility.

family-wage.rationale: Pushed minimum wage increases to $7.25 and spoke of the minimum wage's role in working families' lives.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Voted Nay on the balanced-budget constitutional amendment (S.J.Res. 1) on 27 February and 4 March 1997.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Favoured taxing the wealthy at higher rates and voted to raise the top rate in 2008, which is the opposite of a flat tax.

free-trade.rationale: His trade votes point both ways: Yea on NAFTA (1993), the Uruguay Round authority (1993), permanent normal trade relations with China (2000) and the Peru agreement (2007); Nay on fast track (1991) and on CAFTA (2005).

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Nulled: the only source is an OnTheIssues summary, which is not evidence; no vote or remark of his on owners' freedom to choose whom they deal with was found.

future-generations.rationale: The DNC address insists children and grandchildren inherit an unpolluted, beautiful country.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about protection from discrimination, and the statement now asks only about legal recognition according to gender identity.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Said in 1983 that the best defence against nuclear war is arms control and then disarmament.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Nulled: the only source is an OnTheIssues summary, which is not evidence; the Voteview votes found concern the Social Security surplus, not individual accounts.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Nulled: the only source is an OnTheIssues summary, which is not evidence; no vote or remark of his on whether rights belong only to individuals was found.

job-guarantee.rationale: Spoke in 1980 of increasing the government's commitment to full employment with public employment programmes when necessary.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Voted for the 1999 Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty and for a 1983 nuclear freeze; but also voted in 1999 to deploy national missile defence.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He rejects using civil coercion to impose disputed religious judgments on private conduct.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: Voted Yea on the Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act (April 2001, March 2002), which limits soft money.

limit-guns.rationale: Voted for background checks at gun shows in 1999 and said he had spoken out for gun control.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mixed: in 1980 he spoke of keeping the free enterprise system free in fact, while he backed government programmes such as national health insurance and public employment.

military-superiority.rationale: In 2006 he explicitly favors retaining America’s leading economic and military position against rising rivals.

more-religion-public.rationale: He explicitly welcomes religious contributions to public conscience on genuinely collective moral questions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The DNC speech defends free enterprise and competition through deregulation rather than discarding market capitalism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Consistently backed federal programmes such as health insurance, education and public employment, rejecting a minimal state.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: He rejects treating religious affiliation or nonbelief as qualifications for public office.

party-controls-media.rationale: The speech defends expression and access to ideas against censorship and book burning.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Nulled: the only source is an OnTheIssues summary, which is not evidence; no statement of his on men's structural advantage was found.

positive-liberty.rationale: Argued that equal pay and opportunity, health care and welfare give people real means to use their freedom.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Said in 1980 that the poor have human needs and that health must not condemn people to poverty; opposed welfare cuts.

property-franchise.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about tax or poll-tax qualifications, or no voting at all, and the statement now asks about a property qualification.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Opposed Robert Bork's nomination in 1987 for his view of segregated lunch counters, and opposed segregation.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Said in 2007 the Senate must root out bigotry and prejudice in the country, and argued discrimination remains the obstacle for disabled and minority citizens.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted Yea on the Fair Minimum Wage Act's federal increase (24 and 31 January, 1 February 2007) and Nay on amendments letting states set their own minimum wage.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Nulled: the only source is an OnTheIssues summary, which is not evidence; no vote or remark of his recognising a genocide was found.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Voted for comprehensive immigration reform in 2007 with a guest worker programme and path to citizenship, and defended the 1965 Act's family unification.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Said in 1980 he would tame monopoly, and voted in 2001 and 2002 for bans on corporate and union donations to campaigns.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

religious-nation.rationale: That speech defines Americans’ common membership through freedom and mutual respect across faiths and nonbelief.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted Nay on the Defense of Marriage Act (10 September 1996) and Nay on the Federal Marriage Amendment (7 June 2006), opposing a national ban on recognising same-sex marriage.

school-vouchers.rationale: On the Senate floor (2003-05-07) he said private school vouchers are not proven to work and should not be supported by Congress, and that public funds should be used for public schools.

separate-church-state.rationale: Truth and Tolerance defends institutional separation while allowing religious voices in democratic debate.

separated-powers.rationale: His 2005 oral history defends Senate independence and the constitutional balance against executive encroachment.

single-official-language.rationale: Voted Nay on 6 June 2007 on the amendment declaring English the national language of the United States government, and Nay in 2008 on moving EEOC funds away from cases against employers that require English.

social-market-economy.rationale: The DNC speech combines competitive private enterprise with social insurance, worker protections and progressive taxes.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: His oral history rejects executive circumvention of institutional rules and stresses the rule of law.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The DNC address urges national action to reindustrialize America and revive its inner cities.

state-harmful.rationale: Consistently argued for government programmes such as national health insurance and public employment, which rejects the view that the state is harmful.

strong-leader.rationale: He condemns executive attempts to override Senate procedures and bypass its independent constitutional role.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Spoke against the 2000 Republican bill to repeal the estate tax and voted against repeal in 2006 and against raising the exemption in 2008.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Voted in 2008 to raise the tax rate on income over $1 million and said he would close tax loopholes in 1980.

unions-good.rationale: Sponsored a card-check bill in 2009, voted to restrict employer interference in union organising in 2007, and was rated 100% by the AFL-CIO.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Introduced single-payer national health insurance bills in 1970 and 1979 and called universal coverage the cause of his life; in 2008 he called health care a fundamental right.

voter-id.rationale: Voted Nay on 5 June 2007 and on 19 July 2007 on amendments requiring in-person voters to present photo identification.

war-builds-character.rationale: Said in 1969 that American boys were too valuable to be sacrificed for a false sense of military pride.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Nulled: the only source is a Wikipedia summary, which is not evidence, and no statement of his on withdrawal from public life was found.

women-suffrage.rationale: Joined reintroducing the Equal Rights Amendment (2007-03-27), saying women had to wage a long battle to win the same basic rights granted to men and that the amendment should guarantee them equally.

notes: Third pass (claude-sonnet-5-5). Checked his Senate roll calls on Voteview (minimum wage, DOMA and the marriage amendment, English as national language, gun checks, death penalty, balanced budget amendment, campaign finance, affirmative action, voter ID, NATO enlargement, Iraq, immigration, trade) and his floor speeches in the Congressional Record (Stanford corpus, 1995-2009). Answers that rested only on OnTheIssues or Wikipedia summaries were replaced from those records or nulled, with the earlier answer kept in reviewHistory. Statements his votes and speeches do not settle stay null.
